expected_wrong_value: E: a central diamond aperture plus four additional rectangular exterior corner notches
mechanism: Map the red vertical and blue horizontal discarded-corner ghost legs to the four orthogonal outer corner notches in E, while the actual black diagonal cut still corresponds to the central diamond aperture. Predict double-counting one removed corner depiction as both the true central diamond cut and an extra four-corner right-angle clipping pattern, leading to E. This conflates absent old boundary with additional cut boundaries; the existing dashed ghosts are preserved so a careful reader rejects it.

mathematical_proof.original_geometry: First horizontal half fold sends the bottom half upward. Second vertical half fold sends the left half rightward. The remaining quarter has bottom and left folded edges, and top and right original outer edges. In the final displayed square o104, the absent lower-left vertex (17,7.75) is the intersection of both fold lines.
mathematical_proof.exact_coordinates: Let that centre vertex be (0,0), and normalize original half-side to L=3/2. The cut joins (0,3/4) to (3/4,0), so the removed quarter triangle is x>=0,y>=0,x+y<3/4. Reflecting across x=0 and y=0 gives |x|+|y|<3/4.
mathematical_proof.shape: A single central diamond hole with vertices (+/-3/4,0),(0,+/-3/4). The original four corners (+/-3/2,+/-3/2) survive, since each has |x|+|y|=3>3/4.

all_choices.A: Axis-aligned square aperture has horizontal/vertical sides, not reflected slanted cut edges. Impossible.
all_choices.B: Intact outer square plus one central diamond aperture. Exactly the derived shape.
all_choices.C: No central aperture, and entire outer boundary is a diamond inscribed in the original square. Source central cut cannot remove original corners.
all_choices.D: No central aperture; four outside corner notches. These cannot arise from the central quarter vertex.
all_choices.E: Correct central aperture but additional outside corner notches. Those corners are untouched by the cut.

mathematical_proof.uniqueness: Only B has both the unchanged outer square and exactly the central diamond hole.
mathematical_proof.candidate_color_semantics: Source color is confined to two dashed legs lying strictly in the removed corner except their cut endpoints. They outline absent/discarded material, not the surviving sheet. The actual diagonal cut and all surviving material boundaries remain black. Even a physical-color reading of those discarded edges leaves no finite colored surviving edge to transport. E alone receives new color, and E is already geometrically impossible; other samples, including the unique correct one, remain unmodified. No source fold/cut count, crease style, fill, or option geometry changes.

reference_and_history.current_reference: Current Solid167 C01: two existing source features and two candidate boundary groups are compared with red and blue; no old D color mapping is inherited.
reference_and_history.migration: There is only one true source cut. Rather than inventing two cuts, this design distinguishes the two actual discarded corner traces and compares their directions/roles with existing E aperture or notch edges.
reference_and_history.earlier_r01: r01 uses operation indicators (fold-axis guides for Plane194, motion arrows for Plane245). r02 uses only the two dashed legs of the removed corner. Therefore source geometry-role evidence changes, not just style. R01 pixels and all its output remain immutable.
reference_and_history.old_Plane245_attempt: The old A design compared the actual diagonal cut and one vertical ghost leg with the A central square. This design does not color the actual cut, uses both ghost legs, and compares them with E exterior corner notches while retaining its true central diamond. That is a different receiving geometry and a double-counting hypothesis, not old input relabeling.
reference_and_history.old_Plane194_prescreen: A prior untested prescreen warned that coloring ghost legs could be read as changing the cut. Here source true cut remains solid black, both ghosts remain dashed outside retained material, all four cut-corner constructions remain allowed, and no line is added. The proposed error is explicitly accepting the wrong E inner boundary by discarded-versus-surviving edge confusion.
